label: Lakehouse & Delta Lake
desc: 16 interview questions covering Fundamentals, Lakehouse, Delta Lake, Tables and more.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: Databricks is a unified analytics platform that combines data warehousing, data engineering, and machine learning capabilities on top of Apache Spark, offered as a managed service across AWS, Azure, and GCP.

subs.label: Lakehouse
subs.desc: What is the Databricks Lakehouse?

subs.label: Delta Lake
subs.desc: Delta Lake is an open-source storage format that brings ACID transactions to Apache Spark, enabling reliable and efficient data storage and processing on top of Parquet files plus a transaction log.

subs.label: Tables
subs.desc: Tables can be created using SQL CREATE TABLE statements, the Python DataFrame API (df.write.saveAsTable(...)), or by reading external data sources and registering them in the metastore/Unity Catalog.

subs.label: Data Formats
subs.desc: Supported formats include Parquet, CSV, JSON, ORC, Delta Lake, and various other formats through connectors and Spark's pluggable data source API.

subs.label: Storage
subs.desc: How does Databricks integrate with cloud storage?

subs.label: Maintenance
subs.desc: What is table optimization in Databricks? What is the VACUUM command in Delta Lake?

subs.label: CDC
subs.desc: How do you enable change data capture in Databricks?

label: Clusters, Jobs & Performance
desc: 16 interview questions covering Clusters, SQL Warehouses, Jobs, Integration and more.

subs.label: Clusters
subs.desc: A Databricks cluster is a set of computational resources and configurations on which you run data engineering, analytics, and machine learning workloads — essentially a managed Spark cluster.

subs.label: SQL Warehouses
subs.desc: Databricks SQL is a serverless SQL analytics engine that allows you to query your data lake using standard SQL without managing clusters directly — it runs on SQL warehouses, purpose-built for BI-style query patterns.

subs.label: Jobs
subs.desc: Databricks Jobs lets you orchestrate and schedule automated workflows, including Spark jobs, notebooks, and Python scripts, running on ephemeral job clusters by default.

subs.label: Integration
subs.desc: The Databricks REST API allows you to programmatically interact with Databricks services, including cluster management, job execution, and workspace operations — the basis for most CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code integrations.

subs.label: Performance
subs.desc: Databricks Photon is a high-performance, vectorized execution engine (written in C++) that accelerates Spark SQL and DataFrame queries, reducing query latency compared to the standard JVM-based Spark execution engine.

subs.label: Monitoring
subs.desc: Job monitoring can be done through the Databricks UI (job run history, task-level logs), the REST API, cluster logging, and cloud-native monitoring integrations like CloudWatch (AWS) or Azure Monitor.

subs.label: Workspace
subs.desc: The Databricks Workspace is a collaborative environment where teams can share notebooks, collaborate on projects, browse data via the catalog, and manage clusters and jobs — the main UI surface for the platform.

label: Governance, Security & Advanced Features
desc: 12 interview questions covering Security, Unity Catalog, Data Quality, Notebooks and more.

subs.label: Security
subs.desc: Databricks provides encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access control, network security (VPC/VNet injection, private link), audit logging, and integration with cloud IAM systems for identity and credential management.

subs.label: Unity Catalog
subs.desc: Unity Catalog is a unified data governance solution that provides centralized access control, data discovery, and lineage tracking across Databricks workspaces — a single governance layer instead of per-workspace metastores.

subs.label: Data Quality
subs.desc: Data quality can be managed using Delta Lake constraints (CHECK, NOT NULL), Delta Live Tables expectations, third-party frameworks like Great Expectations, and general data profiling/validation pipelines.

subs.label: Notebooks
subs.desc: Databricks notebooks provide an interactive environment for data analysis, visualization, and collaboration, combining code, text, and visualizations in a single shareable document.

subs.label: Languages
subs.desc: Databricks supports Python, Scala, SQL, and R within the same notebook environment, allowing polyglot data engineering and analysis — including mixing languages across cells in a single notebook.

subs.label: Governance
subs.desc: How do you handle data lineage in Databricks?

subs.label: ML
subs.desc: The Feature Store provides centralized management of ML features, enabling version control, feature reuse across teams/models, and consistent feature engineering between training and serving.

subs.label: Streaming
subs.desc: Databricks supports streaming data through Structured Streaming, enabling real-time processing and continuous data pipelines that use the same DataFrame API as batch jobs.
